:::{#thm-projection-diagonal-bounds}
#### The diagonal of an orthogonal projection matrix lies between 0 and 1

Let $\matr{P}$ be an $n \times n$ [orthogonal projection matrix](#def-projection-matrix) with entries $p_{ij}$.
Then

$$
0 \le p_{ii} \le 1
\qquad \text{for every } i = 1, \dots, n.
$$

:::

:::{.proof}
Since $\matr{P}$ is [idempotent](#def-idempotent-matrix) and [symmetric](#def-symmetric-matrix),
$p_{ij} = p_{ji}$ and $\matr{P}^2 = \matr{P}$.
Compare the $(i, i)$ entries of $\matr{P}^2$ and $\matr{P}$:

$$
\ba
p_{ii}
&= (\matr{P}^2)_{ii}
&& \text{(idempotent)}
\\
&= \sumto{j}{n} p_{ij}\, p_{ji}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \sumto{j}{n} p_{ij}^2
&& \text{(symmetric)}
\\
&= p_{ii}^2 + \sum_{j \ne i} p_{ij}^2.
&& \text{(separate the term } j = i \text{)}
\ea
$$

Each $p_{ij}^2$ is non-negative, so $p_{ii} \ge 0$.
The same equation also gives $p_{ii} \ge p_{ii}^2$,
so $p_{ii}(1 - p_{ii}) \ge 0$.
Since $p_{ii} \ge 0$, this requires $p_{ii} \le 1$.
:::
